full_judgment: 4. As observed above, the petitioner instituted the earlier suit seeking declaration of the simpliciter in the suit lands. The suit was decreed on compromise, in that the plaintiff-opposite parties were not parties and no decree was passed against them as well. The petitioner did not obtain any decree for recovery of khas possession in respect of the suit property. Therefore, there was nothing to be stayed of the judgment and decree passed in the suit. If an executable decree was passed in respect of the properties involved in the subsequent suit the Court may, on such terms as to security or otherwise, as it thinks fit, stay execution of the decree on the prayer of the aggrieved party until the pending suit has been decided.
